newsitem.title: ITALY: Shareholder says CIR lacks transparency.
newsitem.headline: Shareholder says CIR lacks transparency.

text.p: Italian financier Luigi Giribaldi who holds 15.27 percent of industrial holding company CIR, controlled by Carlo De Benedetti, said he believed aspects of the group's dealings lacked transparency.
A statement issued on Giribaldi's behalf after his representative voted against the group's 1996 results said he wanted to find out more about how the company had been run in recent years.
"We are justly interested in checking how the group has been managed in the last few years, where in our view there is more shadow than light," said the statement.
"We think clarity in communications is in the interest of the company and of all its shareholders, among whom ... we have a certain relevance which deserves respect," he added.
During the shareholders' assembly Giribaldi's representative Ezio Gallo, asked whether the group possessed any funds which did not show up in its balance sheet.
Gallo also asked what relations CIR had had with jailed financier Florio Fiorini and his now defunct Swiss holding company Sasea, which collapsed in 1992 under a crushing debt burden.
CIR Managing Director Rodolfo De Benedetti told shareholders "Fiorini never acted as a front-man or trustee of our company."
De Benedetti later told reporters he was surprised by Giribaldi's decision to vote against the company's accounts.

"Nothing has been asked of us, we have had no request (from Giribaldi) to join the board. No proposals have been made to us to which we have replied no," said De Benedetti. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
